sections.content:
31,355 people

were counted on the census as "other skilled trades" in England and Wales in March 2021.

People who do this type of work may engrave jewellery and stoneware, make artificial hairpieces, charge fireworks and munitions with explosive material, make lampshades, wickerwork, toys, dolls, models, candles, artificial flowers, other fancy goods, make patterns for moulds for metal castings, make and tune musical instruments, craft precious metals and stones, and perform other hand craft occupations not elsewhere classified.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "other skilled trades" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "other skilled trades", 12.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "other skilled trades" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "other skilled trades" included:

  • textile process operatives
  • artists
  • furniture makers and other craft woodworkers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "other skilled trades" there were more men than women (70.5% compared with 29.5%).

This means "other skilled trades" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "textiles, printing and other skilled trades".

Men made up 70.5% and women made up 29.5% of "other skilled trades"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "other skilled trades" included:

  • upholsterers
  • photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators
  • estimators, valuers and assessors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "other skilled trades" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "other skilled trades" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "other skilled trades", 12.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (68.5% compared with 31.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (53.8%) than self-employed (46.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
